# What the data-dict export loses: National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH)

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2023` | `2024` | `2025` |
|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 43 | 43 | 47 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 35 | 35 | 39 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 74 | 75 | 79 |
| variables listed by name only (no type the records can support) | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| quantities exported with open range bounds (no valid range recorded) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 43 | 43 | 47 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 172 | 172 | 188 |
| groups (batteries, subjects, sections), not exported | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| links between releases, not exported | 86 | 86 | 86 |
| derived properties (scale signatures), not exported | 29 | 29 | 29 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
